description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 77% at $10^1$ and rising to about 78% at $10^3$. MEND starts at around 66% and increases to roughly 74% at $10^3$, while MEMIT begins slightly higher at about 66% and climbs to approximately 72.5%. FT starts at around 62.5% and shows the steepest growth, reaching about 68.5% at $10^3$. IKE begins at approximately 64.5% and stabilizes near 70% across the range. The Base method remains relatively flat, starting at about 61% and ending at roughly 67%. Overall, ROME demonstrates the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, with MEMIT and MEND showing similar trends but with MEMIT slightly outperforming MEND at lower values and falling behind at higher values.

ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
